text:span.text:span: FA-1 Activity: Applied Software Project Planning & Decision Analysis

office:text.text:p: This activity requires students to apply software project management concepts to their own project by making and justifying key managerial decisions. Students analyse the suitability of a development model, team structure, leadership style, risk response, and prepare a basic project schedule using a Gantt Chart. The task emphasises logical reasoning, practical planning skills, and real-world project understanding.

✔ To Promotes analytical thinking and decision making✔ To Directly applicable to students’ own projects✔ To Covers core Software Project Management concepts✔ To Includes practical planning skill (Gantt Chart)✔ To Avoids unnecessary theoretical writing
Each student must analyse their Django project and justify key managerial decisions using logical reasoning (not theory).Responses must be specific to the project being developed.
office:text.text:h: 🔹 Part A — Life Cycle Justification (Logical Choice)

text:list-item.text:p: Why is this model suitable for your project?
What problems may arise if a different model is used?
Compare briefly with at least one alternative model.

office:text.text:p: If one team member leaves suddenly:

text:list-item.text:p: What project activities will be affected?
How will the team manage the situation?
Identify three possible project risks(technical / schedule / resource / external etc.)
Justify why one risk is more critical than the others.

office:text.text:p: Identify how leadership styles will be applied in the project:

text:list-item.text:p: Directive Style — where strict guidance is required
Collaborative Style — where team participation is needed

office:text.text:p: Provide one realistic project situation for each.
office:text.text:h: 🔹 Part E — Project Schedule using Gantt Chart
office:text.text:p: Prepare a Gantt Chart for your project showing:

text:list-item.text:p: Major project activities(e.g., Requirement Analysis, Design, Development, Testing, Deployment)
Must relate specifically to the your project
Gantt chart may be neatly hand-drawn

Relevant risks, correct prioritisation, logical justification
Correct application of both styles with realistic examples
